01 — Profile

Designing at the
intersection of
soul & structure

A passionate fashion designer and researcher from Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, Jaya Priya A brings together technical precision and creative vision in every collection. Pursuing her M.Sc. in Costume Design & Fashion at PSG College of Arts & Science, she has developed an acclaimed body of work bridging conceptual storytelling, sustainable practice, and couture craftsmanship.

Her work draws deeply from human anatomy, the feminine life cycle, and the natural world — translating philosophical themes into wearable, emotionally resonant garments. She is equally committed to sustainable fashion, with her crochet-based upcycling research published in an international journal.

03 — Collections

The work

Three distinct conceptual collections, each rooted in a deep philosophical narrative — from the anatomy of the soul, to the water cycle as feminine metaphor, to sustainable upcycled couture.

"A soul cloaked in flesh,
veiled by bone,
burning through blood"
Collection 01

F/W 2025 · Kids & Womenswear

Encased Essence— The Soul Within

This collection explores the profound relationship between the soul and the human body, portraying the body as both vessel and reflection of the inner self. Influenced by anatomical elements — muscles, skin, organs — the designs bridge the physical and the spiritual, making fashion a medium of soulful expression beyond mere aesthetics.

Net Fabric Satin Velvet Spandex Denim Kids Wear
"As water sustains Earth,
feminine energy
sustains life."

Autumn / Fall · Womenswear

Cycles of Her— Leganza Collection

The water cycle as a metaphor for feminine energy — constant, fluid, and transformative. Evaporation mirrors women's liberation; condensation, their strength; precipitation, their nurturing power; and collection, their resilience. An A-line ball gown with a structured blazer embellished in stone work captures this poetic duality of softness and power.

Net Fabric High GSM Cotton Ball Gown Stone Work Cancan
"From the depths of the
ocean, a French reverie"

French Collection · Womenswear

Ocean Profound— Coral Reef Collection

A French-inspired collection drawing from the vivid, layered world of coral reefs — their colours, their textures, their ecological fragility. The collection speaks to the delicate balance between beauty and vulnerability, translating the oceanic landscape into structured, expressive silhouettes that celebrate both nature and feminine form.

Structured Silhouettes French Aesthetic Coral Palette Womenswear

04 — Research

Green
Loops

M.Sc. Dissertation · 2025–2026

Exploring sustainable fashion through crochet-based upcycling — transforming industrial knitted textile waste into value-added garments.

Published In
International Journal for Multidisciplinary Research (IJFMR)
Volume 8, Issue 2 · March–April 2026 · Impact Factor 9.24
Presented At
National Conference — KSR College
"Converging Sciences & Style" · February 27, 2026

This research investigates upcycling industrial knitted fabric waste as a sustainable textile management strategy. Waste fabric scraps — typically burned or landfilled — are transformed into hand-crocheted cardigan tops, demonstrating that circular fashion can be both ecologically responsible and creatively compelling.

The Research Process

01Collection of knitted fabric waste from Ganpathy Tex, Tiruppur
02Initial inspection, segregation by type, colour & texture
03Washing, drying, ironing & flattening for preparation
04Marking & cutting into uniform 0.5-inch strips
05Joining, rolling, stretching and hand-twisting into yarn
06Design selection — silhouette, stitch, colour, structure
07Hand crocheting using chain, single & double crochet stitches
08Final finishing — trimming, shaping, edging, quality inspection

Key Findings

87% of survey respondents were aware of sustainable fashion. Consumer research (n=23) found that design (56.5%) is the primary purchase driver, with sustainability (26.1%) rising as a key consideration. All respondents recognised sustainability as at least equally important to fashion trends — indicating a market shift toward responsible consumption.

Crochet, as a low-energy manual technique, proved highly adaptable for converting irregular waste strips into structured, wearable garments. Three complete cardigan tops were developed, each demonstrating distinct stitch patterns, colour arrangements, and silhouette directions — proving the creative and commercial viability of upcycled crochet fashion.
